Hyperliquid Tops 30-Day Perpetual Futures Volume with $240B in Trades According to CryptoRank, Hyperliquid led public chains and ecosystems by perpetual futures volume over the past 30 days, with approximately $240 billion in volume. Arbitrum ranked second with $47.2 billion, followed by Solana with $46 billion, Lighter with $45.6 billion, Ethereum mainnet with $44.9 billion and edgeX with $42.3 billion. — link

Financial Data and Ratings Giant S&P Global to Acquire Smart Contract Security Firm OpenZeppelin S&P Global has entered into an agreement to acquire OpenZeppelin, a leading smart contract security company, as it expands its digital asset risk assessment capabilities into onchain technology. Founded in 2015, OpenZeppelin develops one of the industry's most widely used open-source smart contract libraries and has completed more than 900 security engagements. Following the acquisition, OpenZeppelin will continue to operate under its own name as a separate business unit, led by CEO Demian Brener. Financial terms were not disclosed. — link

Circle’s Arc Mainnet Goes Live as Meme-Token Trading Emerges USDC issuer Circle launched Arc’s public mainnet on Sept. 16, with the Layer 1 blockchain using USDC for transaction fees. Meme-token activity has also emerged on the network. Argus, a popular token launchpad, reported $155.78 million in rolling 24-hour trading volume and $228.54 million in cumulative volume, according to its dashboard snapshot at 12:35 UTC. — link

Just In: SEC Approves Innovation Exemption for Tokenized U.S. Stocks to Trade via Onchain AMMs The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced that it has officially approved a temporary, conditional exemptive framework (the "Innovation Exemption") to allow limited pilot trading of tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks on specific onchain platforms known as Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs). The exemption provides temporary regulatory relief to TSVs, ensuring they are not immediately classified as "exchanges" under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 when offering tokenized equities through permissioned automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools, while also establishing clear guidelines for liquidity providers deploying proprietary capital for market-making support. — link
